axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Firecrawl (the "context API for
AI agents") search/fetch/parse/browser-interaction capabilities as tools for agents.
axes.local_files: Reads and writes no local files — it outputs web page text (markdown/structured JSON) and parsed artifacts (PDF and other documents).
axes.background:
The hosted line lives on Firecrawl's side; the monitor tool family can watch page changes on a schedule on Firecrawl's side and emit diffs/alerts —
that is a "server-side task", not a local background process.
axes.tools:
The full profile registers **27 tools** by default (README wording, including the feedback tool;
the FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK/NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK env vars can trim it):
scrape / search / parse / crawl / map / interact (real-browser clicks·form filling·navigation) /
the monitor family / credit_usage / agent tasks / the developer·gov·research vertical search index families.
The hosted keyless endpoint exposes only 3 (scrape/search/parse); the search-only endpoint is fixed at 9.
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory; interact sessions can continue across calls via scrapeId (official README:
you cannot drive it step by step from within a single client call — each call runs one prompt/code round and hands control back).
axes.permissions:
**The keyless free tier works** (scrape/search/parse three tools, rate-limited); the other tools need an API key.
Three hard rules from the official README: the key never goes into the server URL, never into the agent chat,
only into the client or a secret manager. The OAuth endpoint (/v2/mcp-oauth) uses interactive account connection.

mcp.transport:
**streamable-http** (hosted https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp; plus /v2/mcp-oauth
and /v2/mcp-search endpoints) + **stdio** (npx -y firecrawl-mcp), two lines; the README also mentions SSE support.
Verified: repo README (fetched directly 2026-10-23).
mcp.auth:
Keyless free tier (rate-limited) → API key (Authorization Bearer, configured in the client/secret manager)
→ OAuth interactive connection (/v2/mcp-oauth). The local npx line uses the FIRECRAWL_API_KEY env var.
mcp.scope:
Mostly read (search/fetch/parse/monitor); interact can click and fill forms in a real browser —
the boundary between "reading" and "touching things on a web page" must be gated yourself against the target site's authorization boundaries. No local write surface.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full parameter surface of the 27 tools and the feedback tool's behavior (the README has an inventory and trimming wording, not enumerated item by item)
- Rate/quota numbers for the keyless vs keyed tiers (the README only says rate-limited; per D9 and snapshot discipline no numbers are recorded)
- The functional boundaries of the self-hosted deployment line (README claims support, not verified item by item)
related: Also an official retrieval+fetch server: Exa defaults to a minimal two tools, Firecrawl is a 27-tool full-family surface.
A light-vs-heavy contrast: fetch is reference-level single-page reading, Firecrawl carries the heavy crawl/map/interact surface.
